title: Cross-coupled NMOS-PMOS LC-tank voltage-controlled oscillator
topology: A parallel LC tank (a spiral inductor in parallel with a varactor/switched-capacitor bank for tuning) driven by a cross-coupled transistor pair whose negative resistance cancels the tank's loss resistance to sustain oscillation. The complementary (NMOS-and-PMOS cross-coupled) variant stacks an NMOS cross-coupled pair and a PMOS cross-coupled pair across the same tank, doubling the transconductance delivered per unit bias current versus an NMOS-only (or PMOS-only) cross-coupled pair and improving the achievable phase noise for a given power budget; a tail current source (or, in a current-reuse variant, direct rail connection) sets the total bias current and therefore the oscillation amplitude.
spec_class: PHY-class clock generator — voltage-controlled oscillator for PLL clock synthesis where phase-noise performance is the primary spec (e.g. serdes/PHY reference clock multiplication, RF frequency synthesis), traded against the area cost of the on-chip inductor

pdk_portability.notes: The cross-coupled negative-resistance topology itself is fully portable to any PDK offering matched NMOS/PMOS pairs. The LC tank is the sky130-specific part: sky130 (open-MPW variant) has no characterized inductor or accumulation-mode varactor PCell, so both the spiral inductor (see the sky130-spiral-inductor entry for its physical sizing/modeling methodology) and the tuning capacitor bank must be custom-drawn and characterized against sky130's metal stack and available varactor/MOM-cap structures; the phase-noise/tuning-range targets achievable are therefore bounded by whatever tank Q is achievable in sky130's stack rather than by the cross-coupled-pair topology.

sizing_approach: Choose the tank inductance L to set a practical varactor/capacitor bank size at the target center frequency (f = 1/(2*pi*sqrt(LC))), balancing a larger L (smaller, easier-to-integrate tuning capacitance, but lower self-resonant frequency and more area) against a smaller L (higher achievable Q at a given frequency, but a larger, harder-to-match capacitor bank); size the cross-coupled NMOS/PMOS pair's transconductance to provide negative resistance safely exceeding the tank's loss resistance across process/voltage/temperature corners (a startup-gain margin, typically 3x-4x, to guarantee reliable startup) without so much excess gain that it needlessly degrades phase noise or wastes bias current; size the tail current (or complementary current-reuse bias) to set the oscillation amplitude at the edge of the tank's linear voltage swing, since larger amplitude improves phase noise (per Leeson's model) up to the point of device breakdown/reliability limits.
layout_idioms: differential, symmetric layout of the cross-coupled NMOS and PMOS pairs on a common axis of symmetry with the tank, so both halves of the differential oscillation see matched parasitics
spiral inductor placed with a wide keep-out ring (see sky130-spiral-inductor entry) and any patterned ground shield oriented to avoid coupling into the cross-coupled pair's sensitive tail/bias node
short, symmetric tank-to-cross-coupled-pair routing to minimize parasitic series resistance/inductance that would otherwise directly degrade tank Q and phase noise
guard ring around the VCO core (cross-coupled pair, tail current source, and varactor bank) to isolate it from substrate noise injected by adjacent digital switching circuitry

source.citation: A. Hajimiri and T. H. Lee, "Design issues in CMOS differential LC oscillators," IEEE Journal of Solid-State Circuits, vol. 34, no. 5, pp. 717-724, May 1999.
source.license_or_openness: Peer-reviewed IEEE journal paper cited here for its cross-coupled LC-tank oscillator design methodology and phase-noise analysis only (no figures or text reproduced), per the KB's open-sources sourcing rule. This is one of the foundational references establishing the design tradeoffs (tank Q, negative-resistance margin, bias current vs. phase noise) that essentially all subsequent CMOS LC-VCO literature builds on.

notes: This entry is the LC-tank counterpart to cmos-ring-vco-current-starved: pick this topology when phase-noise spec dominates and the area/complexity cost of a custom-drawn spiral inductor is acceptable, and pick the ring VCO when area, tuning range, or the absence of a characterized inductor process option dominates instead. The tank inductor is exactly the sky130-spiral-inductor entry's octagonal patterned-ground-shield spiral -- consult that entry directly for the inductor's own sizing methodology (Yue & Wong pi-model), Q/self-resonant-frequency tradeoffs, and sky130-specific layout/shuttle caveats before laying out this VCO's tank.
